To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) agent-based modeling is a promising tool for predicting how buildings will perform in use, and that (2) designs that allow for local control, rather than centralized control, are likely to perform better.

(1) buildings are sites where users and technology interact; (2) building occupants can be represented by agents; and (3) agent-based modeling can help designers to create buildings that are more usable and sustainable.

buildings that are designed to be easy to use, with a high degree of user control and a low degree of required interaction with the building system, are likely to be more usable than buildings that are not designed to be easy-to-use, with a lower degree of user control or a higher degree of required interaction.
